investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T12:36:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB endpoint (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because the failure is shared identically across all sibling checks and no evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), the swarm gateway or its ELB is the earliest violated dependency boundary, not any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing the remote-agents feature is unreachable from the production-api environment. Every call to POST /api/agents is failing before agent provisioning can begin, returning HTTP 502 with error code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is an infrastructure-layer failure at the swarm gateway or its AWS ELB, not a bug in the eval runner or expected-output contract. No evidence was produced by any of the three checks, confirming the failure occurs before any agent lifecycle data can be returned.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, confirming the request never reached the agent provisioning layer

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — the 502 is returned before any agent identity data is available
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The AWS ELB fronting the swarm gateway is unhealthy, stopped, or has no healthy targets registered — all three checks hit the same 502 from the same ELB endpoint at overlapping times
[Likely] The swarm gateway service itself is down, crashed, or not listening — the ELB is reachable but forwarding to no healthy backend instances, producing a 502

[Possible] A network policy, security group rule, or VPC routing change has blocked traffic from the production-api to the swarm ELB in us-east-2, causing connection failures that surface as 502 at the API layer
[Possible] The swarm gateway URL or ELB DNS record has changed or expired, causing the production-api to route to a stale or decommissioned endpoint

[Lower likelihood] A deployment or configuration change to the production-api's swarm gateway client configuration (base URL, timeout, auth) caused it to target the wrong or unreachable endpoint — no suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this directly

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T12:37 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm ELB endpoint (*.elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents) was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because every check shares the same failure message and the eval runner calls createAgent as the first step for each probe, the swarm gateway is the single upstream dependency whose unavailability caused all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to go uncollected.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — returned a connection error to POST /api/agents at the time of the eval run. Because the runner branch for remote-agent-state (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) calls createAgent before any state polling can occur, the 502 aborted the probe before any evidence could be written, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be missing. The same gateway failure simultaneously caused the sibling checks remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime to fail with the identical message, confirming a shared upstream dependency failure rather than a check-specific code defect. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition on the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-runtime both carry the identical 502 message and empty evidenceKeys, confirming the failure is not isolated to the remote-agent-state probe branch.
verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — the verifier independently flagged a shared upstream dependency failure across all three sibling check IDs.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId) as the first substantive operation; a 502 at this call prevents all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract requires readyState and state, which are only reachable after a successful agent creation — confirming that a gateway failure at creation time cascades to a total evidence gap.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was unavailable or unhealthy at the time of the eval run, causing POST /api/agents to return 502 for all remote-agent provisioning attempts. This is the most strongly supported cause given the identical error message across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api runtime and the swarm ELB, producing a connection-level error rather than an application-level 5xx from the swarm service itself.
Tertiary — The swarm /v1/agents endpoint was temporarily taken offline (e.g., deployment, scaling event, or health-check failure) causing the ELB to return 502 with no healthy targets.

Lower probability — A misconfiguration or credential change affecting the production-api-to-swarm routing layer that caused the ELB URL to become unreachable specifically for agent provisioning requests.

investigations.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T12:36:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB endpoint (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because the failure is shared identically across all sibling checks and no evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState are all missing), the swarm gateway or its ELB is the earliest violated dependency boundary, not any individual check's logic.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing the remote-agents feature is unreachable from the production-api environment. Every call to POST /api/agents is failing before agent provisioning can begin, returning HTTP 502 with error code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is an infrastructure-layer failure at the swarm gateway or its AWS ELB, not a bug in the eval runner or expected-output contract. No evidence was produced by any of the three checks, confirming the failure occurs before any agent lifecycle data can be returned.

The swarm gateway service was intentionally stopped, redeployed, or scaled to zero at the time of the run, making the ELB return 502 with no healthy backends.

A misconfigured or expired routing rule in the production-api layer caused requests to the swarm gateway URL to fail before reaching the ELB (less likely given the error message explicitly names the ELB URL).

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the 502.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared dependency failure
reproductionSteps.details: If all three still return the same 502 message, the swarm gateway is still unavailable.

reproductionSteps.label: Directly probe the swarm gateway ELB health endpoint from the production-api network context
reproductionSteps.details: Issue a GET or HEAD request to the redacted ELB URL (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com) to determine if the load balancer itself is reachable and returning healthy responses.

reproductionSteps.label: Check AWS ELB target group health in us-east-2 for the swarm gateway
reproductionSteps.details: In the AWS console or via CLI, inspect the target group associated with the ELB to see if any targets are healthy at the time of the failure.

recommendedNextActions: Verify current swarm gateway ELB health in us-east-2 by re-running the eval suite and checking AWS target group status before assuming the issue is resolved.
Pull production-api server logs for POST /api/agents between 2026-08-31T12:37:00Z and 2026-08-31T12:37:35Z to determine whether the 502 was isolated to the eval probe or affected other callers.

Check AWS CloudWatch metrics and ELB access logs for the us-east-2 swarm gateway ELB around the failure window to identify whether targets were unhealthy, the service was restarting, or a network event occurred.

If the gateway was transiently unavailable, add a retry or backoff to the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) to distinguish transient blips from sustained outages in future eval runs.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required:true (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 183–184) and degradedAfterFailures is 1, confirm whether the feature health status was automatically marked degraded and whether on-call was notified.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) from the swarm gateway ELB at the same time as the eval failure would disprove gateway unavailability and point to an eval configuration or authentication issue instead.

If the remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state checks passed in a concurrent or immediately subsequent run while remote-agent-runtime still failed, the failure would be isolated to the runtime check rather than the shared gateway.

AWS ELB access logs or CloudWatch metrics showing healthy target responses during the 12:37 UTC window would disprove the gateway-down hypothesis and suggest a routing or proxy misconfiguration in the production-api layer.
A passing run of any remote-agents check within the same eval window would indicate the 502 was transient and not a sustained gateway outage.
Evidence that the ELB URL or routing configuration changed between runs (e.g., a deployment event) would shift the cause from gateway unavailability to a misconfiguration regression.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB health endpoint (GET /health or equivalent) independently of agent creation, so gateway availability can be confirmed before the full agent lifecycle checks run.

Add a gateway-reachability pre-check that runs before remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime; if it fails, skip the downstream checks and surface a single clear gateway-unavailable signal rather than three identical failures.
Add a latency-trend eval for POST /api/agents that tracks p50/p95 response times over time, enabling detection of degraded gateway performance before it reaches full 502 failure.

Consider adding a historical baseline eval that alerts when the same error message appears across all sibling checks simultaneously, as this pattern strongly indicates a shared dependency failure rather than individual check regressions.
